[b]Restoring the Seagates[/b]

Following the Sikirskian Civil War and the collapse of Sal-Baliz, SummitONE Solutions was forced to scale back its Seagates project, a network of privately operated ports that once dotted various sections of Shamat. In the months leading up to SummitONEs entry into the Qianxun market, however, its corporate assets have returned to a level not seen since the opening of its Elseyrian offices during the geopolitical conflict against the Hochdeutsche. And, with the company now poised to create its own stake in Qianxuns Project 661, SummitONEs Board of Directors has decided that now was the time to reactivate its Seagates.

First and foremost, Seagate Austmark on Austmark Island. While the Seagate actually finished construction and has since remained operational, it was left completely devoid of military capabilities due to funds being rerouted to fund military contractors in Sikirsk. Nowadays the Seagate is a state-owned enterprise managed jointly between SummitONE and Norrhollows Department of the Interior, though Almstedt has expressed interest in fully reacquiring a 100% stake in the Seagate, with SummitONE officials arriving at Norrhollow to negotiate the sale of the port back to corporate hands. Vespurian central authorities would also be invited to the talks to act as third-party observers.

Next was the SummitONE base at Seagate Zurekdal in Shamats Wadi Zurayq region, which acted as the companys forward operating base to funnel resources into the Sal-Baliz insurgency. When that conflict was forcibly ended by THEP forces, Seagate Zurekdal was hurriedly evacuated and its documents burned to hide the companys involvement with terrorism. The Board of Directors itself had cautioned against reactivating the base, though Xavier Almstedt would nevertheless push through with reoccupying the site, reasoning that with capital being injected into their Qianxun offices, SummitONE was more than capable of taking a few more reputational hits while nevertheless maintaining its current operational costs.

As both Seagates were relatively brand new, SummitONE is expected to only spend a few million dollars on maintenance and clean-up, though the presence of unwanted Shamatine settlers at Seagate Zurekdal would cause some concern within the Board of Directors, who would approve the creation of an expulsion squad of around 60 men led by operations manager Ulf White to forcibly remove the settlers from the Seagate.

Unbeknownst to the world at large, the coordination of these two projects would actually be directed by the Socialist Ethics Commission of Qianxun in conjunction with the Project 661 Directorate, with Director-General Kang Hongxin himself personally attending the session of the SummitONE Board of Directors. Furthermore, around a quarter of the declared budget listed in SummitONEs accounts would belong to investors associated with Qianxuns Central Bank, who had agreed to lend capital at the insistence of the Min Zhu Politburo, who believe that the reopening of Seagate Zurekdal and militarization of Seagate Austmark are to be key in the liberation of Qianxun from the shackles of its landlocked geography.
